alice.s: Heads-up — found a pretty reproducible issue where the SDK shim strips route-policy TTL and the console shows weird quota attribution :bug:
benj: omg, saw that too when running canary tests this morning :eyes: can you paste a minimal repro?
alice.s: repro curl below. note the header is JSON-ish in TS and python clients, but seems to get flattened in the proxy:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'x-rw-route-policy: {"policy":"soft-affinity","ttl":300}' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
camille.k: repro looks right. on py client we serialize RoutePolicy as header via `headers["x-rw-route-policy"] = json.dumps(route)` — are we URL-encoding anywhere downstream?
diego_r: console mapping expects `route.policy` and `route.ttl_s` fields, so if header arrives as `{policy:..., ttl:300}` the console normalizer fails and we end up attributing to the default bucket. that's why quota usage shows 0 for test tenant.
benj: hmm TS client does `headers.set("x-rw-route-policy", JSON.stringify(route))` too. suspect proxy or shim removes numeric suffix or coerces keys to camelCase?
alice.s: quick trace: python client -> internal proxy -> shim -> route-service. Logs show header value present at proxy ingress, but after shim it's "policy":"soft-affinity","ttl_s":null (ttl lost) :thinking_face:
camille.k: I can look at python logic, but if shim is the culprit we need to coordinate across runtimes. propose bugbash Friday 11:00am PST. attendees: eng-runtime, devex, console.
diego_r: I'll open a console issue and add mapping hotfix (fallback to ttl if ttl_s missing) — low-risk patch.
benj: I'll prepare TS client test and a tiny shim integration test. drafting PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/clients/pull/XXXX (WIP)
alice.s: Camille, can you own the py client side? If shim injects a normalization step we might need to support both `ttl` and `ttl_s` for a while.
camille.k: Yep, I'll add dual-key support and unit tests. also will add header validation in client to avoid sending malformed route objects.
benj: Agree on dual-key approach. For rollout UX: console should show a banner when route header normalization mismatch is detected — call out tenants affected.
diego_r: I'll add banner draft to the console issue. Also adding a telemetry event `route_policy_normalizer_miss` with fields: `client_lang`, `route_keys_present` so we can measure impact.
alice.s: telemetry event sounds good. please keep payload small. we should avoid PII.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: shim-v2 -> canary group (5%) at 2026-06-12T18:00:00Z. Will report health after 15m.
benj: After canary, we'll run the synthetic that hits tenant-qa and check quota attribution and the new telemetry event counts.
camille.k: Plan for Friday bugbash: 11:00-11:45 PST. Agenda: quick triage, assign fixes (py/ts/shim/console), merge hotfixes, kick canary.
diego_r: I'll own console hotfix + banner. benj you own TS tests + PR. camille you own py changes. alice you'll coordinate the canary and validation run?
alice.s: yep. will do final validation and post summary in #eng-platform when complete. thanks all :thumbsup:
benj: shall we add a note to release notes about temporary dual-key support? ops/customer-success might need to know.
diego_r: yes — short blurb: "Console compatibility fix for route-policy TTL key normalization; clients will accept both ttl and ttl_s during migration."
camille.k: pushed a draft branch for py: `py-client/routepolicy-dualkey` (link in PR when ready)
alice.s: ok locking schedule. if anyone hits blockers ping me @alice.s.
benj: +1. good catch.
camille.k: :rocket:
